On the Government of Cities

Chapter I

The government of a city differs from that of a household in kind and not merely in degree, as has often been argued since Aristotle.

He said that the city comes into being for the sake of life, and continues in being for the sake of the good life. This formula has been repeated so often that its difficulty is easily missed.

Chapter II

In the first place, the magistrate is not a father. According to the civilians, his authority is derived and not natural, and may therefore be resumed by those who conferred it.

For example, the practice of the Italian republics shows that a magistracy may be annual without being weak.
